insp.title: Channel
insp.knob.tip: {0}: {1} (drag or use the wheel · double click: {2})
insp.empty.b: (or the record button) and the new channel lands right here on the timeline.
insp.empty.c: You can also import an audio file from “New track”.
insp.transpose.hint: Same length, so it stays in sync with the video. The first time takes a few seconds; then it is kept in the project.
insp.transpose.tip: Changes the track's pitch without changing its length, so it stays in sync with the video. Double click the value to go back to the original.
transpose.error: I couldn't transpose “{0}”: {1}. It keeps sounding as recorded.
tl.media.videoOff: Audio + video (this track isn't in the video: turn on "In the video" to show its panel)
insp.inVideo.tip: The track has its panel in the video. Turn it off to make it sound only (a backing track, a click…)
insp.sat.hint: How hard the channel pushes into the tube or the tape. It is calibrated to the channel level
insp.sat.tape.hint: Tightens the hits, smooths harsh highs and adds a bit of body to the lows.
insp.sat.tube.hint: Even harmonics: warmer and rounder, peaks soften without losing sparkle.
insp.comp.manual.tip: Hand-set values: pick a style to go back to the simple control
insp.comp.amount.tip: Amount: {0}. Moves everything together (compression, attack, release, EQ) and keeps the volume even (drag or use the wheel · double click: medium)
insp.comp.rhythm.hint: Rhythm and riffs: evens out the hits, keeps the pick attack and leaves room for the lead
insp.comp.arpeggio.hint: Arpeggios and clean tones: evens out the strings, soft notes are heard and it sounds open
insp.comp.lead.hint: Solos and melodies: more sustain, even notes and presence so it sits up front
insp.comp.makeup.hint: Make-up: makes up for the volume the compression takes away
insp.comp.presence.hint: Positive: the guitar comes forward. Negative: leaves room for another one
insp.comp.limit.tip: A limiter after the compressor catches pick hits and loud notes
insp.comp.fine.hint: Moving these values switches the compressor to “Manual”. Pick a style to go back to the simple control.
insp.reverb.hint: How much of this track goes to the reverb bus (after the fader)
insp.delay.hint: How much of this track goes to the delay bus (after the fader)
insp.sync.offset.hint: Fixes this channel’s audio sync (negative = earlier). Includes the latency compensation; the timeline snap respects it
insp.sync.camera.hint: Makes up for the camera delay so the fingers match the audio
insp.clip.reset: Restore clip (no trims, fades or volume changes)
insp.clip.gain.hint: Raises or lowers this clip before the channel. To change the volume in parts, click the line of the selected clip to add points
insp.clip.trimStart.hint: Hides the start of the channel without moving the rest
insp.clip.linkFades: The video follows the audio fades
insp.clip.linkFades.tip: The video fades to black along with the volume
insp.clip.hint: On the timeline: drag the clip to move it, its edges to trim and the top corners for fades.
insp.frame.hint: Drag the panel in the video to move the framing; the mouse wheel zooms.
insp.removeClip.hint: The file stays saved; you can use it again from History.
insp.none.hint: Click a track or its panel in the video.
insp.none.empty: No channels recorded yet. The guitar is waiting.

grid.fixed.hint: Always one line every {0}, at any zoom
snap.clips.name: Snap to other clips
snap.clips.on.tip: Snap to other clips: {0}. The nearest magnet wins, grid or edge (Alt: free)
snap.clips.off.tip: Snap to other clips: off. Pick which edge of the clip you move sticks to the others' edges
snap.clips.hint.start: The clip's start sticks to a nearby clip's edge
snap.clips.hint.end: The clip's end sticks to a nearby clip's edge
snap.clips.hint.both: The clip's start or end sticks to a nearby clip's edge

sc.loopOut: A–B range end at the playhead

menu.loopRange.tip: Uses it as the A–B range and turns the loop on.
err.loop.short: The loop range is too short.
range.deleted: Deleted {0:0.00} s from the range: the gap stays and nothing else moved. You can undo it.
range.nothing: There was nothing to delete in that range.

color.adj.whites.hint: The brightest parts: brighter or duller

color.tpl.empty: Save the filter, adjustments and effects as a template to use in other projects.

mix.eq.rhythm.hint: Removes muddy lows and a bit of mud at 250 Hz
mix.eq.lead.hint: Tames the harsh part (3–4 kHz) and cuts the fizz on top
mix.eq.acoustic.hint: Less body boom, a bit of sparkle
mix.eq.front.hint: More presence so the guitar sits up front
mix.delay.preset.Slapback.hint: A single short bounce, rockabilly / country
mix.delay.preset.Punteada.hint: Dotted eighth: the classic for arpeggios and leads
mix.delay.preset.Ping-pong.hint: Quarter notes bouncing between left and right
mix.delay.preset.Ambiente.hint: Long and dark, a backdrop for slow solos
mixer.title: MIXER
mixer.width.auto.tip: Wide channels when they fit (2–3 channels), compact if there are many
mixer.pan.tip: Pan templates for every track with a take
mixer.pan.width.tip: How wide the tracks end up with the template
mixer.empty: Record a channel to see it in the mixer.
mixer.emptyTag.tip: Empty track: the next channel you record here takes these settings
mix.comp.tip: Compression {0}: {1} (style and limiter in the Channel tab)
mix.sat.knob.tip: Life: how hard the channel pushes into the tube or the tape (double click: 30%)
mix.lim.on: Peak limiter on: catches pick hits and loud notes
mix.lim.off: Peak limiter off: catches pick hits and loud notes
mix.comp.knob.manual: Compressor in Manual: pick a style to use this knob
mix.comp.knob.tip: Amount of compression (wheel or drag · double click: medium)
mix.gr.tip: How much the compressor (and limiter) is lowering the volume right now
mix.slot.menu.tip: Move, repeat or remove this effect
mix.slot.drag.tip: Drag to change the order of the chain
mix.slot.duplicate.tip: Another one with the same settings, right after it
mix.slot.remove.tip: It stops sounding and leaves the strip. If it was the only one of its kind, turning it on from the Channel tab brings it back (so does Ctrl+Z)
mix.slot.add.tip: Add another effect at the end of this track's chain
mix.slot.add.comp: One more compressor, with its styles
mix.reverb.knob.tip: Reverb send (wheel or drag · double click: 0)
mix.delay.knob.tip: Delay send (wheel or drag · double click: 0)
mix.reverb.info.tip: The reverb sound is set in the Reverb channel, on the right
mix.delay.info.tip: The delay sound is set in the Delay channel, on the right
mix.transpose.reset.tip: Double click: back to the original pitch
mix.hint.reverb.pre: Pre-delay: gap between the direct sound and the reverb
mix.hint.reverb.lowcut: Low cut at the reverb input
mix.hint.delay.repeats: Feedback: how many repeats you hear
mix.hint.delay.tone: Brightness of the repeats (each one comes out darker than the last)
mix.hint.delay.lowcut: Low cut on the repeats so they don’t get muddy
mix.hint.delay.duck: Lowers the repeats while you play and lets them ring in the silences
mix.delay.stereo.tip: Stereo: each side repeats on itself (the right one a bit later)
mix.delay.pingpong.tip: Ping-pong: the repeats bounce between left and right
mix.master.lim.tip: Master limiter: lights up when it is working. Set it in the Master card
master.open.tip: Open mastering: cleanup, multiband compressor, color and limiter
master.title: Master
master.on.tip: Turn the whole master on or off
master.eq.lowcut.tip: Low cut: removes the deep rumble you can't hear but takes up room
master.eq.mud.tip: Mud (300 Hz): lower it if the mix sounds muddy or boxy
master.eq.lows.tip: Lows (100 Hz): more or less body at the bottom
master.eq.presence.tip: Presence (3 kHz): guitar further forward or back
master.eq.air.tip: Air (10 kHz): sparkle and air on top
master.eq.tilt.tip: Tilt: the whole mix brighter (+) or darker (−), pivoting at 1 kHz
master.bands.on.tip: Turn the multiband compressor on or off
master.band.low.tip: How much to compress the lows: evens them out without pumping. It adjusts to your mix's level by itself
master.band.mid.tip: How much to compress the mids, where the guitar lives: glues and evens it
master.band.high.tip: How much to compress the highs: tames pick attacks and cymbals
master.gr.tip: How much this band is compressing right now
master.cross.tip: The three bands and how much each one is compressing. Drag the lines to move where the lows end and the highs begin (Shift for fine steps; double click resets)
master.stage.clean.tip: Before compressing: removes what's extra at the bottom and the mud
master.stage.color.tip: After compressing: the mix's color, without the compressor squashing it
master.stage.tape.tip: Tape saturation over the whole mix: glues it and warms it up
master.tape.amount.tip: How much tape: a little glues the mix, a lot dirties it
master.width.tip: 100% = as it is; less narrows it toward mono, more widens it
master.monobass.tip: Below this frequency everything goes to the middle: the lows don't get lost on a phone or a single speaker
master.stage.clip.tip: Rounds the fastest peaks (the pick, the strum's attack) before the limiter, so it squashes less
master.clip.amount.tip: How much of the peaks the soft clip takes instead of the limiter. On Auto (0) it only steps in on the hottest peaks: it takes a share (up to 4 dB) and leaves the rest to the limiter, so it pumps less
master.clip.gr.tip: What it is clipping right now
master.stage.meter.tip: How the mix comes out. It starts over each time you press play
master.meter.int.tip: Integrated LUFS since you pressed play: what YouTube, Instagram and TikTok look at
master.meter.peak.tip: The highest peak since you pressed play, counting what happens between samples (dBTP). In red, it went over the ceiling: the video can clip it
master.meter.togo.tip: How much it is short of (+) or over (−) the Target's loudness (with no target, −14 LUFS, the social media one)
master.target.tip: Where it will play: the mix is heard (and exported) at the loudness that platform plays it at. It measures on its own after each change
master.target.none: No target: it goes out at the loudness it has.
master.target.failed: I couldn't measure the mix. I'll try again with the next change.
master.look.tip: A starting point for the master, picked by ear. "Amount" moves all of it; then you can touch each knob
master.look.custom.tip: The knobs as you left them
master.look.natural.tip: Gentle glue and a little cleanup: it hardly changes the colour
master.look.glue.tip: Everything tighter and closer: the bands work harder and the tape rounds it off
master.look.bright.tip: More air and presence, with the highs held a bit more so it doesn't sting
master.look.warm.tip: More lows and tape, and a softer top
master.look.front.tip: The mids forward: presence, less mud, narrower and the lows in mono
master.look.pick.tip: Pulls 2 to 5 kHz down only when the pick hits; the rest stays the same
master.look.amount.tip: From Natural (0) to the whole look (100 %). On Natural, from nothing to Natural
master.suggest.tip: Listens to the whole mix and suggests EQ, per-band compression and Pick. It shows what it would do and you apply it
master.suggest.wait: Some audio is still loading or being transposed: try Suggest in a moment.
master.suggest.empty: There is nothing to listen to yet: record or import a take.
master.suggest.failed: I couldn't listen to the mix: {0}
master.suggest.title: Here's my take
master.band.pick.tip: The fourth band: pulls 2 to 5 kHz down only when the pick hits, fast, and leaves the sustained tone as it is
master.band.pick.gr.tip: What it is pulling down right now
suggest.lowcut: Low cut at {0} Hz, just in case.
suggest.lowcut.rumble: Low cut at {0} Hz: there's rumble at the very bottom.
suggest.mud: Mud {0}: too much between 250 and 500 Hz.
suggest.presence.up: Presence {0}: it sits a little back.
suggest.bands: Multiband {0} / {1} / {2} %: by how spiky each band is.
suggest.pick: Pick at {0} %: the attacks sting between 2 and 5 kHz.
suggest.even: The mix is even: the colour hardly needs touching.
master.stage.lim.tip: The last step: no peak goes over the ceiling. Off, peaks can go over 0 dB and clip
master.lim.drive.tip: How hard you push the mix into the limiter: more drive, more loudness and more squash. With a Target, it sets it
master.lim.ceiling.tip: How high the peaks go, counting what happens between samples (dBTP). −1 dB by default, what social media asks for: it leaves room for the video's compression
master.lim.release.tip: How fast it lets go: short sounds louder, long more natural
master.lim.gr.tip: What the limiter is taking off right now
master.status.off: Off: the mix goes straight to the output
master.status.on: On: the mix goes through the chain from left to right
master.out.note: Always last, with the master on or off

main.saveRetry: I couldn’t save: {0}. I’ll try again…

unsaved.saveFail: I couldn’t save, so I’m not closing: check the bell to see why. To quit anyway, pick “Close without saving”.
main.noVideo: No video (is the file, ffmpeg or ffprobe missing?): {0}
main.restoredNoView: I recovered the settings, but couldn’t update the view: {0}

set.panel.tip: Open the driver’s panel to change the buffer size. When the driver changes it, I reopen the audio by myself.
set.mode.mono1.tip: Input 1 only, duplicated to both sides
set.mode.mono2.tip: Input 2 only, duplicated to both sides
set.gain.hint: Affects the meter and the recorded WAV
set.monitor: Monitor the input through this output
set.monitor.tip: Turn it on only if your interface has no direct monitoring (it adds latency)
toast.test.title: To try
toast.camera.lost: The camera dropped out. Check that it is connected and press “Refresh devices” in Settings.
toast.audio.lost: The audio interface ({0}) stopped responding. Check that it is connected and pick it again in Settings.
ver.title: Go back to a saved version
ver.tip: Versions are saved on their own while you work. Going back to one keeps what you have now as another version.
ver.none: No saved versions yet: they are saved on their own while you work.
ver.restored: I went back to the version from {0}. What you had before was kept as another version, in case you want it back.
ver.fail: I couldn’t go back to that version: {0}. The project is as it was.
set.transportFade.hint: Avoids the click when you play or stop. Shorter is tighter, longer is softer (10 ms is fine almost always)
set.fine.hint: Added to the latency (calibrated or estimated). Negative = the new channel sits earlier
set.camLatency.hint: How late the image arrives compared to the audio
set.panelFail: I couldn’t open the driver’s panel: {0}
set.shortcut.taken: {0} used to be "{1}": now it is "{2}".
set.cal.tap.error: I didn’t detect enough hits. Play a short, muted note on every click, loudly and without letting it ring.
set.cal.loop.error: The signal didn’t come back. Check that the cable goes from the output to an input of the interface (or the microphone is in front of the speaker) and that the gain isn’t at its minimum.
set.locked: It can’t be changed while you record or calibrate.
set.output.help: The tracks, the click and the monitoring play through here. Use the interface’s output for the lowest latency. Each input and output pair keeps its own calibration.
set.lat.parts: output {0} ms + input {1} ms, according to the driver
set.lat.auto: · it is compensated automatically on every new channel
set.lat.high: The output has a lot of latency: Bluetooth headphones, HDMI or an external speaker? Listen through the interface’s output.
set.lat.stale: The audio setup has changed since you calibrated (sample rate or output device). It is best to calibrate again.
set.cal.title: Calibrate latency
set.cal.useEstimate.tip: Discard the measurement and use what the driver reports
set.cal.cableHow: Connect a cable from the interface’s output to an input (or put a microphone in front of the speaker). Turn the headphones down: 8 noise pulses will play.
set.cal.tapHow: Listen to 4 count-in clicks and then play a short, muted note right on each of the next 12. It is less precise than the cable.
set.cal.help.can: Measures the real latency. A cable from the output to an input is the most precise; otherwise, play along with the click.
set.cal.help.cant: Open the audio interface (and don’t be recording) to calibrate.
set.cal.varied: The measurements varied quite a lot. Repeat it{0}.
set.sc.help: Click a shortcut and press the new key (with Ctrl, Shift or Alt if you like). Esc cancels. If the key belonged to another action, that one is left without a shortcut. Esc always cancels the count-in and whatever you are dragging.
set.sc.wheel.help: The plain wheel scrolls up and down. Click one and turn the wheel while holding Ctrl, Shift or Alt (or two of them). Esc cancels.
set.sc.wheel.press.tip: Hold Ctrl, Shift or Alt and turn the wheel (Esc: cancel)
set.sc.wheel.reverse.tip: Turns the wheel direction around for this gesture, leaving the others alone

proj.pick.none: I didn’t find a GuitarCam project in that folder. To create a new one, pick an empty folder.
proj.pick.several: That folder holds several projects ({0}): pick the folder of the one you want to open.
proj.pick.web: That project is from the web version of GuitarCam and this version can’t open it. To bring it over: create a new one, copy what’s in takes\ into its media\ folder and open it again; the takes show up with their video in History.
proj.pick.root: Pick where to save new projects
proj.empty.none: You don’t have any projects yet. Create one with "New project".
proj.saveTemplate.tip: Save as a template (tracks, channels, effects, format and color)
proj.tpl.name: Template name
proj.nameTaken: There is already another project with that name.
proj.trashAsk.b: to the Recycle Bin? All of its channels and exports go with it.
exp.folder.reset.tip: Back to the project’s exports folder
exp.mp3.tip: 320 kbps: light, for sending or uploading.
exp.q.std.tip: Very good quality and a lighter file (CRF 22).
exp.fileGone: The file is no longer in that location (it was moved or deleted).
exp.needTrack: You need at least one channel on the timeline to export.
exp.needVideo: There are no takes with video to build the MP4. Record with the camera or import a video; if you only want the sound, switch to Audio only at the top.
exp.pick.audio: Pick where to save the audio
exp.pick.video: Pick where to save the video
exp.mp3.note: 320 kbps MP3: light, for sending or uploading.
exp.wav.note: Lossless 24-bit WAV: to keep editing or mastering.
exp.stems: Also each track in its own WAV (stems)
exp.stems.tip: Leaves a «name - stems» folder next to it, with one WAV per track that plays: each with its effects and sends, without the master limiter, all from 0 so they line up in another program
exp.adv.tip: Resolution and bitrate by hand. Leave it alone and it comes out as always
exp.adv.bitrate.auto.tip: The quality picks it for the frame size
exp.adv.bitrate.autoHint: The quality picks it. On the processor the quality rules and the size follows the picture; move the slider to set it yourself.
exp.adv.bitrate.customHint: More bitrate, more sharpness and a bigger file. For social media 8–16 Mbps is enough at 1080p, and 35–45 at 4K.
exp.folderGone: That folder no longer exists. Pick another one.
exp.exists: There is already a {0}{1} in that folder: it will be replaced.
exp.target.desc: {0}×{1} · {2}. The project stays as it is.
exp.loudness.target: The mix goes out at {0} LUFS: the master's Target ({1}), as you hear it.
exp.loudness.asis: The mix goes out at the loudness it has. To bring it to a platform's, pick the Target on the master.
exp.loudness.tip: The loudness is picked on the master (Mastering → Volume → Target), so you hear it while mixing
exp.done.lufs.tip: LUFS: the mix's integrated loudness (EBU R128), measured like the master's LUFS cell. The tail is the reverb and delay still ringing after the last clip
about.desc: For making guitar videos: you record channels with camera and audio, mix them and export a video with one panel per channel.
about.settings: Your settings, recent projects and templates are in your user folder.
about.settings.tip: Show the settings folder in Explorer
rec.openAudio: Open the audio interface to see its inputs.
rec.readOnly: The project is open read-only: I can’t record here.
rec.noneArmed: No track is armed: arm one with its ● (or create one from “New track”) and record.
rec.noCamera: The camera isn’t sending an image: this channel will be audio only.
rec.noVideoTrack: No armed track goes in the video: I won’t record the camera this time.
rec.videoFail: I couldn’t record the video ({0}): this channel will be audio only.
rec.closeFail: I couldn’t close the channel: {0}. What was recorded comes back when you open the project.
rec.diskFail: There was a problem writing the channel to disk: {0}
rec.dropped: {0} ms of audio were lost on the channel (the disk couldn’t keep up)
rec.videoProblem: There was a problem recording the video: {0}
rec.noImage: No image came from the camera: the channel ended up audio only.
rec.discarded.many: I discarded the channels: the files went to the Recycle Bin in case you need them.
rec.discarded.one: I discarded the channel: the file went to the Recycle Bin in case you need it.
rec.timelineFail: I couldn’t put "{0}" on the timeline; the recording is safe and comes back when you open the project.
rec.saveFail: I couldn’t save the channel: {0}. I’ll try again…
imp.title: Import audio
imp.busy: I can’t import right now: finish what you’re doing and try again.
imp.unknown: I can’t read "{0}": try WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A or AIFF.
imp.switched: I couldn’t add "{0}" to the timeline because you switched projects; it stayed in the media/ folder.
imp.done.one: I imported the audio and put it on a new track.
imp.done.many: I imported {0} audio files, each on its own track.
eq.reset.tip: Put this band back as it was (off)
eq.q.tip: Higher = narrower bell (to hunt for an annoying frequency); lower = wider and more musical
eq.help: Drag the points on the graph. While it plays, you see this track’s spectrum behind.
eq.graph.tip: Drag a point (Shift = fine) · wheel: bell width / cut slope · double click a point: turn on/off · double click elsewhere: new band
engine.cantCalibrate: It can’t be calibrated while you record.
tempo.tip: Drag up/down (whole or decimal) · mouse wheel (Shift = fine) · double click to type
tempo.name: Tempo in BPM
tempo.tap: Tap the rhythm to measure the tempo
live.title: LIVE
theme.title: Theme
err.asio.notFound: I couldn't find the ASIO driver "{0}".
err.asio.none: There are no ASIO drivers installed.
err.asio.noOpen: None of the ASIO drivers would open. Is the interface plugged in?
err.export.noTracks: You need at least one channel on the timeline to export.
err.export.replace: Couldn't replace {0}: it may be open in another program.
camera.errIp: We couldn't connect to the DroidCam direct stream at {0}. Check that the IP and port (4747) match the ones the phone app shows, and that the DroidCam PC client is closed.
camera.errDroid: DroidCam Video is selected but sends no picture. Make sure the DroidCam Client program is open on Windows with the video running ("Start"), or switch to the "DroidCam IP mode" button above.
err.import.format: I can't read "{0}": try WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, M4A or AIFF.
err.clip.clipNotFound: I couldn't find that clip in the project.
err.clip.swapNotFound: I couldn't find the clip to swap with.
err.clip.mediaNotFound: I couldn't find that channel in the history.
err.clip.mediaInUse: That channel is already on the timeline.
err.clip.splitEdge: The playhead has to be inside the clip, more than 0.1 s from its edges.
err.sync.number: The sync adjustment has to be a valid number.
err.aspect: The aspect ratio has to be 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1.
err.layout: The layout has to be side-by-side or top-to-bottom.
err.lib.notEmpty: That folder isn't empty. Pick an empty folder to create the project.
err.lib.notProject: That folder isn't a GuitarCam project
err.lib.open: It's open in another GuitarCam window
store.notProject: The file isn't a GuitarCam project
store.newer: It was saved by a newer version of GuitarCam: opened read-only
store.noProject: The folder has no GuitarCam project
store.damaged: The project was damaged: I opened it from {0}
store.damagedKept: The damaged file was kept as {0}
store.locked: It's open in another GuitarCam window: opened read-only
store.missing: Audio files are missing: {0} (they stay offline)
store.orphan: {0} clip(s) point to media that isn't in the project
store.recovered: I recovered the interrupted recording "{0}" ({1:0.0} s)
store.adopted: There were {0} file(s) in media/ that the project didn't have: I added them to the media ({1})
look.icon.none.tip: Show the track number instead of an icon
icon.speaker: Speaker
menu.folder.hint: Groups tracks: drag them into the folder by their handle. Its fader, M and S act on all of them.
preset.menu.hint: A new track with a sound you saved: effects, pan, color, icon and input.
preset.none: You haven't saved any yet. Right-click a track → Save as preset.
preset.save.tip: Saves this track's effects, pan, color, icon and input to add it in other projects.
preset.save.note: Same name replaces the one you had.
preset.saved: Saved the preset “{0}”. Find it in New track → Preset.
folder.remove.tip: I'll ask whether its tracks go too.
folder.remove.only.tip: Its tracks stay where they are, out of the folder.
folder.remove.all.tip: The takes stay in the project, and Undo brings them back.
track.remove.yes.tip: The takes stay in the project, and Undo brings it back.
folder.color.tracks.ask: Paint its {0} tracks with this color too?
folder.color.tracks.ask1: Paint its track with this color too?
folder.color.tracks.tip: Gives the folder's tracks the color you just picked (you can undo it)
folder.mix.hint: The folder's volume, Mute and Solo act on all its tracks together, without touching each one's own.
mixer.folder.fold: Fold: leave only the folder's channel
mixer.folder.fader.tip: Whole folder volume: moves all its tracks together
mixer.folderTag.tip: This channel rules all the folder's tracks: its fader, M and S
err.preset.name: Give it a name.
set.view.knobs.help: The ones shown in each track's header on the timeline when you make it taller. All of them by default; turn off the ones you know you won't use and the rest get more room.
set.save.onEdit.tip: Every change saves itself right away
set.save.interval.tip: Collects your changes and saves them every so often
set.save.onEdit.help: Everything you touch is saved a second and a half later. The safest option, though you'll often see "Saving".
set.save.interval.help: Changes wait and are saved every {0} min. Meanwhile the top bar says "Unsaved"; the disk at the top saves them sooner.
set.save.manual.help: Saves when you press {0} or the disk at the top. Meanwhile it says "Unsaved": if the computer hangs, you lose what you didn't save.
set.save.manual.help.nokey: Saves when you click the disk at the top. Meanwhile it says "Unsaved": if the computer hangs, you lose what you didn't save.
set.save.always: Takes, exports and switching projects always save, whatever you pick. If you close with unsaved changes, I ask first.
set.encoder.gpu.tip: NVIDIA, AMD or Intel: much faster, and it leaves the processor free for the effects
set.encoder.cpu.tip: Slower, but the file is smaller at the same quality
set.encoder.found: Found a {0} card: the video is encoded there. If it ever fails, the export carries on with the processor.
set.encoder.none: I couldn't find an NVIDIA, AMD or Intel card FFmpeg can use, so the video is encoded on the processor.
set.encoder.cpu.help: The video is encoded on the processor (x264): it takes longer and the computer works flat out meanwhile, but the file comes out lighter.
sc.deleteClose: Delete the range and close the gap
tools.name: Timeline tools
tool.select.tip: Select: move, trim and pick clips (Shift+drag marks a range)
tool.range.tip: Range: drag to mark a stretch, over several tracks too; right-click to delete it
tool.split.tip: Split: a click on a clip cuts it there (with snap, on the grid; with Alt, free)
tool.erase.tip: Erase: a click removes the clip; dragging removes every clip you touch
tool.listen.tip: Listen: hold the button on a clip to hear that track alone from there
tool.zoom.tip: Zoom: a click zooms in, Alt+click zooms out and a drag shows just that stretch
tool.hand.tip: Hand: drag to move the view
menu.deleteRangeClose.tip: Removes the stretch and slides what follows on these tracks to fill it. Other tracks and the markers stay put
range.closed: I deleted {0:0.00} s and slid what follows to close the gap. You can undo it.
trans.title: Transition
trans.audioOnly: Crossfades one clip's audio into the other, using the sound the trims hide.
trans.audioShort: Neither clip has hidden audio on the other side: the sound crosses with a quick fade right at the join.
trans.cut.tip: Goes straight from one clip to the other, as before.
trans.crossfade.tip: One picture blends into the other and so does the sound: half before the join and half after.
trans.dip.tip: The picture fades to black up to the join and the other clip fades in; the sound crossfades.
trans.length.tip: How long the transition lasts, centered on the join. Double-click the value to go back to 0.5 s.
trans.audio: The audio fades too, using the sound the trims hide. Each clip's own fades don't change.
trans.still.out: The outgoing clip has no more video after the join: it holds its last frame.
trans.still.in: The incoming clip has no video before the join: it holds its first frame.
trans.still.both: Neither clip has hidden video on the other side: each one holds its edge frame.
menu.toFront.tip: Where this clip overlaps another one on the track, this one shows (in the preview and the exported video). The sound doesn't change
split.edge: I can't cut there: at least 0.1 s of clip has to stay on each side.
listen.noAudio: Listening needs the audio on: pick the interface in Settings.
sc.paste: Paste the clips at the playhead
menu.paste.tip: Pastes what you copied, starting at the playhead, with its top track on this one.
clipboard.pick: Pick the clip you want to copy (or box several).
clipboard.copied: Clip copied: put the playhead where it goes and paste it with {1}.
clipboard.copied.many: {0} clips copied: put the playhead where they go and paste them with {1}.
clipboard.cut: Clip cut: put the playhead where it goes and paste it with {1}.
clipboard.cut.many: {0} clips cut: put the playhead where they go and paste them with {1}.
clipboard.empty: Nothing copied yet: pick a clip and copy it with {0}.
err.clip.pasteOtherProject: Those clips are from another project: copy them again here.
err.clip.pasteNoMedia: The take of one of those clips is gone.
err.clip.pasteTracks: Those clips span {0} tracks and the project has {1}.
